> **Session focus:** *Mastering the Triangle of Statistical Communication and perfecting consultation endings*

## Learning Objectives

* Understand and apply the Triangle of Statistical Communication (Listening/Paraphrasing/Summarizing, Asking Great Questions, Explaining Statistical Ideas)
* Recognize the central importance of relationship in successful collaborations
* Master techniques for ending consultations effectively
* Practice complete consultations using the ASCCR framework

---

## Description of Activities

The morning explored the Triangle of Statistical Communication, emphasizing how listening, questioning, and explaining form interdependent communication skills. We examined how relationship quality underpins all successful collaborations. The extended afternoon session focused on ending consultations effectively, including summarization, action planning, and feedback solicitation. We observed recorded consultations using the ASCCR framework, analyzing strengths and areas for improvement through structured class discussions.

---

## Reflection (Gibbs Reflective Cycle)

### 1. Description

The Triangle of Statistical Communication revealed communication as multifaceted—requiring active listening and strategic questioning, not just clear explanations. The relationship discussion emphasized trust-building over time rather than single interactions. The ending practices showed how proper closure ensures mutual understanding and commitment to next steps. Observing real consultations allowed us to see the ASCCR framework applied holistically.

### 2. Feelings

The communication triangle validated my suspicion that I'd been over-emphasizing explanation at the expense of listening and questioning. The relationship focus felt both obvious and revolutionary—obvious because all human interactions depend on relationships, revolutionary because statistical training rarely addresses this. Watching recorded consultations was simultaneously encouraging (seeing experienced statisticians also struggle) and intimidating (realizing the skill level required).

### 3. Evaluation

The triangle model effectively balanced different communication modes, preventing over-reliance on any single approach. The relationship emphasis correctly identified it as foundational rather than supplementary. The ending techniques addressed a common weakness—consultations that drift off rather than concluding decisively. Video observation provided insights impossible to gain from description alone.

### 4. Analysis

Effective statistical communication requires code-switching between technical and lay vocabularies while maintaining precision. Relationship-building in professional contexts differs from social relationships—it requires demonstrating competence, reliability, and genuine interest in collaborators' success. Proper endings prevent the common problem of misaligned expectations that surface weeks later. The video observations revealed that even experienced practitioners must consciously apply these principles—they don't become automatic.

### 5. Conclusion

This day demonstrated that communication and relationship skills are not "soft" additions to technical expertise but fundamental competencies that enable statistical knowledge to create impact. Without these skills, even brilliant statistical insights may fail to influence research or practice.

### 6. Action Plan

I will practice the "listening-first" approach in my next consultation, consciously waiting before offering solutions. I'll develop a repertoire of relationship-building practices appropriate for different collaboration contexts. I'll create an "ending checklist" to ensure consistent consultation closure. I'll also begin recording my consultations (with permission) for self-review.
